input.headline: Corporate spreads widen: member default risk and surveillance rise
input.what_happened: The 20-day widening of the Baa corporate bond spread over the 10-year Treasury yield reached 11 bp on Nov 5.
input.so_what_front: Wider credit spreads can signal rising member default risk, increasing the demands on FICC surveillance and default-management preparedness.
input.so_now_what_front: Brief FICC and NSCC credit surveillance teams on any members showing stress signals.
input.action_reason: S is elevated at 4; early briefing of surveillance teams is appropriate before stress can develop further.
